subject: mathematics
question_text: If A is the matrix with rows (1, 1, 3), (5, 2, 6) and (−2, −1, −3), then find A³.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.46, chapter 5 MATRICES, Short Answer question 18(ii). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+2+1 shape puts half the marks on A³ because it can only be reached after A² and so carries the compounding risk — an error in A² is invisible until A³ comes out wrong — and keeps a whole mark for the second route A·A², because the answer here is the zero matrix and a student who reaches O by a slip has no other way to tell. The same 1+2+1 is used on the neighbouring A³ card in this unit. Independently computed before authoring, both ways: A² has rows (0, 0, 0), (3, 3, 9) and (−1, −1, −3); A²·A gives the 3×3 zero matrix and A·A² gives the 3×3 zero matrix, so the two routes agree. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Matrices supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find A³ — say what you work out first, how you use it, and how you check the answer.

steps.label: Find A²
steps.margin_note: First mark. Multiply row by column, watching the negatives. Row 1 against column 1 is 1 + 5 − 6 = 0, and the whole first row of A² turns out to be zero.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply row by column, watching the negatives: row 1 against column 1 is 1 + 5 − 6 = 0.
lines: The whole first row of A² is zero.

recall.must_convey: That A² is A multiplied by itself, row against column, and that the first row of the result comes out all zeros.
accept: A squared is A times A by row into column multiplication
multiply the matrix by itself and the first row comes out all zeros
work out A into A carefully because of the negative entries
A square ante A into A, row into column multiply cheyyali
find the product of A with itself first

steps.why: A³ is built from A², so this matrix is used again in the next step. A row of zeros appearing here is a strong hint about what A³ will be, and it is worth checking one entry twice before going on.
common_mistakes: Squaring each entry instead of multiplying the matrices.
Dropping a minus sign when a negative entry meets a negative entry.

steps.label: Find A³
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. A³ = A²·A — use the matrix just found, not A three times over. Row 1 of A² is zero, so row 1 of A³ is zero without any work; the other six entries all cancel.
steps.memory_tip: A³ = A²·A. A zero row in A² stays a zero row in the product, so only six entries need working out.
lines: Row 1 of A² is zero, so row 1 of A³ is zero.

recall.must_convey: That A³ is found as A² multiplied by A, reusing the matrix already computed, and that every entry of the product comes out zero.
accept: A cubed is A squared times A so multiply the matrix already found by A
use A squared and multiply it by A again and every entry becomes zero
the product of A squared and A is the zero matrix
A cube ante A square ni A tho multiply cheyyali, anni zeros vasthai
multiply the previous result by A once more and it all cancels

steps.why: Matrix multiplication is associative, so A·A·A can be grouped as (A·A)·A. Reusing A² halves the work, and that is why the steps are in this order.
common_mistakes: Multiplying A by A by A from scratch and making a fresh arithmetic error.
Writing the answer as 0 instead of O — the answer is a matrix, not a number.
Sign slips: 3 + 15 − 18 is 0, but 3 + 15 + 18 is not.

steps.label: Check with A·A²
steps.margin_note: Last mark. A zero answer is easy to reach by mistake, so multiply the other way round as well. Row 1 of A is (1, 1, 3) and column 1 of A² is (0, 3, −1), giving 0 + 3 − 3 = 0.
steps.memory_tip: A zero answer is easy to reach by a slip, so multiply the other way round and confirm it.
lines: Matrix multiplication is associative, so A·A²
must give the same answer. Row 1 of A is

recall.must_convey: That the answer is checked by computing A·A² as well, that this gives the zero matrix too, and that A³ is therefore O.
accept: check by working out A times A squared and it also gives the zero matrix
multiplication is associative so A into A squared must match and it does
the second route gives all zeros as well so A cubed is O
A ni A square tho multiply chesina kuda zero matrix ne vasthundi
confirm the zero answer by multiplying in the other grouping

steps.why: The zero matrix is the one answer an arithmetic slip is most likely to produce by accident, since a single wrong entry can cancel everything. Doing the product the other way round is a cheap independent test.
common_mistakes: Accepting a zero answer without any check.
Writing "A³ = 0" instead of "A³ = O", the zero matrix.
